On November 2, 2015, Entergy Arkansas, Inc. (EAi) (formerly Arkansas Power 
and Light Company) submitted in this docket an ANO Decommissioning Cost Rider 
NDCR Update (Update) and the Supplemental Testimony and Exhibits of Barbara L. 
Casey. On December 1, 2015, the General Staff (Staff) of the Arkansas Public Service 
Commission (Commission) submitted the Direct Testimony of Kim 0. Davis. 
Positions of the Parties 
Ms. Casey explains EA.I's 2015 annual update to its Arkansas Nuclear One (ANO) 
Decommissioning Cost Rider (Rider NDCR). Casey Supplemental at 3-4. She states 
that Rider NDCR is an exact recovery rider that recovers a levelized-real (inflation 
adjusted) revenue requirement necessary to fund the decommissioning trusts for ANO 
Units 1 and 2. Id. at 5. 
Ms. Casey testifies that for Unit 1 of ANO, based on the 2015 inputs, there is 
projected to be an accumulated excess trust fund balance of $120.8 million, once the 
decommissioning process is complete in 2046. Id. at 5. She testifies, however, that the 
balance for Unit 2 is projected to be insufficient by $248.0 million. Id. at 5-6. Ms. 
Casey explains that these estimates are based on current assumptions as to trust fund 
earnings rates, trustee and investment management fees, nuclear cost escalation rates,

the Decommissioning Cost Estimate (2014 dollars) filed on March 31, 2014 in this 
docket, and the currently approved Nuclear Regulatory Commission license expiration 
dates of 2034 and 2038 for ANO Unit 1 and ANO Unit 2, respectively. Id. at 6. 
Ms. Casey notes that the projected ANO Unit 2 trust fund balance after 
decommissioning has dropped from a positive balance of $320 million in 2013, to $7 
million in 2014, to a $248 million insufficiency in 2015. Id. at 7-8. Ms. Casey attributes 
this trend to three factors: (1) the Commission-approved estimate for decommissioning 
costs for Units 1 and 2, which is revised every five years, rose from $1,050 million in 
2009 to $1,344 million in 2014; (2) the cost of decommissioning is assumed to escalate 
at a rate equivalent to the Consumer Price Index-Urban (CPI-U), which has trended 
upward; and (3) the performance of the trust funds over the last year was lower than in 
2014, with the Unit 2 projected balance falling from $330.3 million in 2014 to $313.6 
million in 2015. Id. at 6 and 8. 
Mr. Casey testifies that the Rider NDCR decommissioning revenue requirement 
for 2016 is $2. 71 million. 
Id. at 9. 
She estimates that the bill impact of the 
redetermination on a typical residential customer using 1,000 kWh per month is an 
increase of $0.16, or 0.15 percent. Id. 
Mr. Davis reviews and confirms the above testimony and notes that the current 
rates for ANO Unit 2 are zero for each rate class. Davis Direct at 6. He states that EAi's 
redetermination filing shows a zero revenue requirement for ANO Unit 1 and a $2.714 
million revenue requirement for ANO Unit 2 for 2016. Id. at 7. Mr. Davis states that 
the primary driver of the rate increase is the increased projected decommissioning cost, 
approved by Commission Order No. 61 in this docket on November 10, 2014. Id. He

also notes that the currently-approved nuclear decommissioning cost estimate does not 
include post-shutdown spent fuel management costs. Id. at 4. 
Having reviewed EAI's application, testimony, and workpapers, Mr. Davis 
recommends continued suspension for 2016 for Unit 1 and approval of a revenue 
requirement of $2. 714 million for Unit 2, with collections to begin for the Rider NDCR 
in January 2016. Mr. Davis thus recommends approval of the tariff rates reflected in 
Attachment A to Rate Schedule No. 37 (Attachment 1, page 1of3, of EAI's November 2, 
2015 filing). 
Findings and Rulings 
On the basis of EAI's tariff filing and the testimony of Ms. Casey, and of Mr. 
Davis's review and recommendations, the Commission finds that EAI's update of Rider 
NDCR as filed on November 2, 2015, is consistent with the public interest. Accordingly, 
the Commission approves the following: 
(1) continued suspension for 2016 of the Unit 1 component of the rate for Rider 
NDCR Unit 1; and 
(2) a revenue requirement of $2.714 million for Unit 2; and 
(3) the tariff rates reflected in Attachment A to Rate Schedule No. 37 (Attachment 
1, page 1 of 3, of EAI's November 2, 2015 filing), with collections to begin for 
Rider NDCR in January 2016.
